help.(top):
Description:

Usage:
  cyclonedx [command] [options]

Options:
  --version       Show version information
  -?, -h, --help  Show help and usage information

Commands:
  add                         Add information to a BOM (currently supports files)
  analyze                     Analyze a BOM file
  convert                     Convert between different BOM formats
  diff <from-file> <to-file>  Generate a BOM diff
  keygen                      Generates an RSA public/private key pair for BOM signing
  merge                       Merge two or more BOMs
  sign                        Sign a BOM or file
  validate                    Validate a BOM
  verify                      Verify signatures for BOMs and files
help.validate:
Description:
  Validate a BOM

Usage:
  cyclonedx validate [options]

Options:
  --input-file <input-file>                                  Input BOM filename, will read from stdin if no value provided.
  --input-format <autodetect|json|xml>                       Specify input file format.
  --input-version <v1_0|v1_1|v1_2|v1_3|v1_4|v1_5|v1_6|v1_7>  Specify input file specification version (defaults to v1.7)
  --fail-on-errors                                           Fail on validation errors (return a non-zero exit code)
  -?, -h, --help                                             Show help and usage information

help.(top):
Semantic SBOM diff and analysis tool

Usage: sbom-tools [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  diff                 Compare two SBOMs
  view                 View a single SBOM
  validate             Validate an SBOM against a compliance standard
  rules                List the compliance rules each standard checks, or explain one rule
  diff-multi           Compare a baseline SBOM against multiple targets (1:N comparison)
  timeline             Analyze SBOM evolution over time (timeline comparison)
  matrix               Compare all SBOMs against each other (`NxN` matrix comparison)
  quality              Assess SBOM quality and completeness
  query                Search for components across multiple SBOMs
  vex                  Standalone VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange) operations
  watch                Continuously monitor SBOMs for file changes and new vulnerabilities
  completions          Generate shell completions
  config-schema        Generate JSON Schema for the config file format
  config               Show, discover, or initialize configuration
  verify               Verify SBOM integrity
  cache                Manage the enrichment cache (status, warm, clear, export, import)
  license-check        Check license policy compliance
  enrich               Enrich an SBOM with vulnerability and EOL data
  tailor               Tailor (filter) an SBOM by removing unwanted components
  merge                Merge two SBOMs into one
  convert              Convert an SBOM to another format (e.g. SPDX → CycloneDX)
  cra-docs             Generate CRA technical-documentation dossier (Annex V templates)
  cra-standards-watch  Show curated CRA standards-watch catalogue (prEN, BSI, CSAF, EUCC, …)
  man                  Generate a man page and print it to stdout
  help                 Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose
          Enable verbose output

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --no-color
          Disable colored output (also respects `NO_COLOR` env)

      --export-template <EXPORT_TEMPLATE>
          Export filename template for TUI exports
          
          Placeholders: {date}, {time}, {format}, {command}

      --config <CONFIG>
          Path to configuration file

      --no-config
          Skip config-file discovery entirely (ignore any `.sbom-tools.yaml`)

      --offline
          Offline mode: never make network calls; enrichment is served purely from cache (including TTL-expired entries, with a staleness warning). For air-gapped environments. Also settable via `SBOM_TOOLS_OFFLINE` (accepted values, case-insensitive: 1/0, true/false, yes/no, on/off)
          
          [env: SBOM_TOOLS_OFFLINE=1]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

EXIT CODES:
    0  Success / gate passed
    1  Gate failed: --fail-on-change, --min-score, --fail-on-noncompliant,
       validate errors or --fail-on findings (or N/A under
       --require-applicable), query with no matches, vex status/filter
       --actionable-only, verify audit-hashes gate
    2  Vulnerabilities introduced (diff/view --fail-on-vuln); compliance
       warnings (validate --fail-on-warning)
    3  Usage error (unknown flag or value, missing argument) or operational
       error (I/O, parse, config, invalid values)
    4  VEX gaps found (--fail-on-vex-gap)
    5  License policy violations found (license-check)
    6  Actively exploited (KEV) vulnerability introduced (--fail-on-kev)
    7  ML performance metric regressed (diff --fail-on-ml-regression)

EXAMPLES:
  Comparing SBOMs:
    sbom-tools diff old.cdx.json new.cdx.json                     # Interactive TUI
    sbom-tools diff old.cdx.json new.cdx.json -o summary           # Terminal summary
    sbom-tools diff old.cdx.json new.cdx.json -o json > diff.json  # JSON export
    sbom-tools diff old.cdx.json new.cdx.json -o sarif             # CI/CD SARIF

  Enrichment (add vulnerability + EOL + KEV data before diffing):
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --enrich-vulns --enrich-eol
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --enrich-vulns --kev
    sbom-tools view app.cdx.json --enrich-vulns --fail-on-vuln

  CI/CD pipeline gates:
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --fail-on-vuln --fail-on-change
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --enrich-vulns --kev --fail-on-kev
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --fail-on-vex-gap --vex vex.json
    sbom-tools quality app.cdx.json --min-score 70

  Fleet / multi-SBOM analysis (interactive TUI or -o json):
    sbom-tools diff-multi baseline.json device-*.json -o json
    sbom-tools timeline v1.json v2.json v3.json --enrich-vulns
    sbom-tools matrix *.cdx.json --cluster-threshold 0.9

  Search and query:
    sbom-tools query "log4j" --version "<2.17.0" fleet/*.json
    sbom-tools query --affected-by CVE-2021-44228 *.json

  Quality and compliance:
    sbom-tools quality app.cdx.json --profile security --metrics
    sbom-tools validate app.cdx.json --standard ntia,cra,eo14028
    sbom-tools rules --standard cra                # What a standard checks
    sbom-tools rules explain SBOM-CRA-ART-24       # One rule in full
    sbom-tools license-check app.cdx.json --strict

  VEX operations:
    sbom-tools vex status app.json --vex vex.json
    sbom-tools vex apply app.json --vex vex.json -O enriched.json

  SBOM operations (enrich, filter, merge):
    sbom-tools enrich app.cdx.json --enrich-vulns --enrich-eol -O enriched.json
    sbom-tools tailor app.cdx.json --exclude-ecosystems npm,pypi
    sbom-tools merge primary.json secondary.json -O combined.json

  Monitoring:
    sbom-tools watch --dir ./sboms --enrich-vulns --exit-on-change
    sbom-tools verify hash app.cdx.json --hash-file app.cdx.json.sha256

For more details on any command: sbom-tools <command> --help
help.diff:
Compare two SBOMs

Usage: sbom-tools diff [OPTIONS] <OLD> <NEW>

Arguments:
  <OLD>
          Path to the old/baseline SBOM

  <NEW>
          Path to the new SBOM

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output format (auto detects TTY: tui if interactive, summary otherwise)

          Possible values:
          - auto:         Auto-detect: TUI if TTY, summary otherwise
          - tui:          Interactive TUI display
          - side-by-side: Side-by-side terminal diff (like difftastic)
          - json:         Structured JSON output
          - sarif:        SARIF 2.1.0 for CI/CD
          - oscal-json:   OSCAL 1.2.3 assessment-results JSON
          - markdown:     Human-readable Markdown
          - html:         Interactive HTML report
          - summary:      Brief summary output
          - table:        Compact table for terminal (colored)
          - csv:          CSV for spreadsheet import
          - ndjson:       Newline-delimited JSON (one record per line, streaming-friendly)
          - sbomqs-json:  interlynk-io/sbomqs v2.1.2 `score --legacy --json`-shaped quality scores (0-10), recomputed per-feature for side-by-side comparison with sbomqs output (`quality` command only)
          
          [default: auto]

  -v, --verbose
          Enable verbose output

  -O, --output-file <OUTPUT_FILE>
          Output file path (stdout if not specified)

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress non-essential output

      --no-color
          Disable colored output (also respects `NO_COLOR` env)

      --sarif-base <DIR>
          Directory the SBOM path in `-o sarif` output is relative to. Defaults to the repository the SBOM file is in (the nearest ancestor holding a `.git`), else the current directory. Only `-o sarif` reads it

      --export-template <EXPORT_TEMPLATE>
          Export filename template for TUI exports
          
          Placeholders: {date}, {time}, {format}, {command}

      --sarif-category <CATEGORY>
          Code-scanning category of `-o sarif` output (its `automationDetails.id`). Defaults to one per command and standard set or profile, such as `sbom-tools/cra+ntia/`; give each SBOM its own when one workflow uploads results for several SBOMs checked the same way. Only `-o sarif` reads it

      --config <CONFIG>
          Path to configuration file

      --sarif-max-results <N>
          The most results one `-o sarif` run keeps (default 25000, the most GitHub code scanning accepts; 0 keeps every result). Beyond it the least severe are omitted, with a warning in the run and on stderr. Only `-o sarif` reads it

      --no-config
          Skip config-file discovery entirely (ignore any `.sbom-tools.yaml`)

      --reports <REPORTS>
          Report types to include

          Possible values:
          - all:             All report types
          - components:      Component changes summary
          - dependencies:    Dependency changes
          - licenses:        License changes
          - vulnerabilities: Vulnerability changes
          
          [default: all]

      --fuzzy-preset <FUZZY_PRESET>
          Fuzzy matching preset

          Possible values:
          - strict:           Strict matching (fewer false positives)
          - balanced:         Balanced matching (default)
          - permissive:       Permissive matching (fewer false negatives)
          - strict-multi:     Strict matching optimized for multi-SBOM comparison
          - balanced-multi:   Balanced matching optimized for multi-SBOM comparison
          - security-focused: Security-focused matching
          
          [default: balanced]

      --offline
          Offline mode: never make network calls; enrichment is served purely from cache (including TTL-expired entries, with a staleness warning). For air-gapped environments. Also settable via `SBOM_TOOLS_OFFLINE` (accepted values, case-insensitive: 1/0, true/false, yes/no, on/off)
          
          [env: SBOM_TOOLS_OFFLINE=1]

      --include-unchanged
          Include unchanged components in output

      --fail-on-vuln
          Exit with code 2 if new vulnerabilities are introduced

      --fail-on-kev
          Exit with code 6 if any introduced vulnerability is in CISA's KEV catalog (implies --kev enrichment)

      --fail-on-change
          Exit with code 1 if any changes detected (without this flag, changes still exit 0)

      --only-changes
          Only show items with changes (hide unchanged)

      --severity <SEVERITY>
          Filter by minimum severity (critical, high, medium, low)

      --enrich-vulns
          Enable OSV vulnerability enrichment

      --enrich-eol
          Enable end-of-life detection via endoflife.date

      --kev
          Flag vulnerabilities in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog

      --epss
          Annotate vulnerabilities with FIRST EPSS exploit-probability scores

      --enrich-staleness
          Detect stale/abandoned/deprecated dependencies via package registries

      --huggingface
          Enrich ML-model components from the HuggingFace Hub (weight hashes from `siblings[].lfs.sha256`, task from `pipeline_tag`, license, staleness)

      --vex <PATH>
          Apply external VEX document(s) (OpenVEX format). Can be specified multiple times

      --vuln-cache-dir <VULN_CACHE_DIR>
          Cache directory for enrichment data

      --vuln-cache-ttl <VULN_CACHE_TTL>
          Cache TTL in hours
          
          [default: 24]

      --refresh-vulns
          Bypass cache and fetch fresh data

      --api-timeout <API_TIMEOUT>
          API timeout in seconds
          
          [default: 30]

      --matching-rules <MATCHING_RULES>
          Custom matching rules YAML file

      --graph-diff
          Enable graph-aware diffing (detect reparenting, depth changes)

      --graph-max-depth <GRAPH_MAX_DEPTH>
          Maximum depth for graph analysis (0 = unlimited, requires --graph-diff)
          
          [default: 0]

      --graph-impact-threshold <GRAPH_IMPACT_THRESHOLD>
          Minimum impact level to include in graph diff output (low, medium, high, critical)
          
          [default: low]
          [possible values: low, medium, high, critical]

      --graph-relations <GRAPH_RELATIONS>
          Comma-separated list of relationship types to include in graph diff (e.g., "DependsOn,DevDependsOn"). Empty = all types

      --dry-run-rules
          Dry-run matching rules (show what would match without applying)

      --ecosystem-rules <ECOSYSTEM_RULES>
          Path to ecosystem rules configuration file (YAML/JSON)
          
          [env: SBOM_TOOLS_ECOSYSTEM_RULES=]

      --no-ecosystem-rules
          Disable ecosystem-specific name normalization

      --exclude-vex-resolved
          Exclude vulnerabilities with VEX status `not_affected` or fixed

      --fail-on-vex-gap
          Exit with code 4 if introduced vulnerabilities lack VEX statements (CI gate)

      --fail-on-ml-regression
          Exit with code 7 if a supported ML performance metric regresses.
          
          Higher is better: accuracy, f1, precision, recall, auc, roc_auc, bleu, rouge. Lower is better: loss, error, perplexity, latency.

      --detect-typosquats
          Enable typosquat detection warnings

      --explain-matches
          Show detailed match explanations for each matched component

      --recommend-threshold
          Recommend optimal matching threshold based on the SBOMs

      --streaming
          Force streaming mode for large SBOM handling (reduces memory usage)

      --streaming-threshold <STREAMING_THRESHOLD>
          Streaming threshold in MB. Files larger than this use streaming mode
          
          [default: 10]

      --cra-product-class <CLASS>
          CRA Annex III/IV product class (drives severity calibration of the CRA Phase 1 and Phase 2 checks). One of: default, important-class-1, important-class-2, critical. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2392 gives the technical description of each class's product categories. A CRA sidecar's `productClass` wins over this flag

      --as-of <DATETIME>
          Pin the evaluation clock (RFC 3339, e.g. 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z or 2027-01-01). Deadline-sensitive checks (CRA Art. 14 readiness, SBOM age, EUCC certificate expiry, PQC deadlines) and the quality score evaluate against this instant instead of the wall clock — reproducible CI runs

      --pqc-mode <MODE>
          How the CNSA 2.0 and NIST PQC checks judge quantum-vulnerable cryptography: readiness (default) makes every such algorithm an error; deadline judges each by its migration deadline at --as-of (NIST IR 8547: info until it is deprecated after 2030, warning until it is disallowed after 2035, error after; the CNSA 2.0 timeline for cnsa2) and records the deadline on the finding

          Possible values:
          - readiness: Today's strict view: every quantum-vulnerable algorithm is an error
          - deadline:  By the migration calendar at the evaluation date: each finding names its deadline and the schedule that sets it

      --pqc-profile <PROFILE>
          With --pqc-mode deadline, whose deadlines the NIST PQC check applies: nist (default, NIST IR 8547) or federal (also EO 14412 / OMB M-26-15 for high value assets and high impact systems: PQC key establishment by 2030-12-31, PQC signatures by 2031-12-31, TLS 1.3 by 2030-01-02)

          Possible values:
          - nist:    NIST IR 8547: deprecated after 2030, disallowed after 2035
          - federal: IR 8547 plus the federal deadlines for high value assets and high impact systems (EO 14412, OMB M-26-15)

      --cnsa-category <CATEGORY>
          With --pqc-mode deadline, the CNSA 2.0 equipment category whose timeline the CNSA 2.0 check applies (when CNSA 2.0 is to be preferred, and when it is to be used exclusively). Unset: the strictest, software-signing (2025, 2030)

          Possible values:
          - software-signing:  Software and firmware signing: preferred by 2025, exclusive by 2030
          - web-cloud:         Web browsers, servers and cloud services: preferred by 2025, exclusive by 2033
          - networking:        Traditional networking equipment (VPNs, routers): preferred by 2026, exclusive by 2030
          - operating-systems: Operating systems: preferred by 2027, exclusive by 2033
          - niche:             Niche equipment (constrained devices, large PKI systems): preferred by 2030, exclusive by 2033
          - custom-legacy:     Custom applications and legacy equipment: updated or replaced by 2033

      --rule <RULE=SETTING>
          Set a rule's severity for this run, or turn it off: RULE=off|info|warning|error, e.g. --rule SBOM-NTIA-SUPPLIER=warning (repeatable; `sbom-tools rules` lists the rule ids). The verdict, the counts, the score and the exit code follow the severities it sets; each finding keeps the severity its check gave it as `default_severity`. `off` drops the rule's findings and counts them under `suppressed`. Wins over the config file's `compliance.rules` for its rule

      --include-excluded-scope
          Judge components whose scope is excluded by the package rules too (version, supplier, license, hash, identifier, dependency graph). CycloneDX `scope: excluded` (and an SPDX development, build or test dependency) marks a component the product does not need at runtime; by default those are left out, and each result says how many

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

EXIT CODES:
    0  Success (changes alone exit 0 without --fail-on-change)
    1  Changes detected (--fail-on-change)
    2  Vulnerabilities introduced (--fail-on-vuln)
    3  Usage error (unknown flag or value, missing argument) or operational
       error (I/O, parse, config, invalid values)
    4  VEX gaps found (--fail-on-vex-gap)
    6  Actively exploited (KEV) vulnerability introduced (--fail-on-kev)
    7  ML performance metric regressed (--fail-on-ml-regression)

EXAMPLES:
    sbom-tools diff old.cdx.json new.cdx.json                    # Interactive TUI
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json -o summary --fail-on-vuln   # CI gate
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --enrich-vulns -o sarif     # Enriched SARIF
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --graph-diff --graph-max-depth 3
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --enrich-vulns --kev --fail-on-kev
    sbom-tools diff old.json new.json --vex vex.json --fail-on-vex-gap

sbom-tools.version_output:
sbom-tools 0.4.0

Supported SBOM Formats:
  CycloneDX: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7 (JSON, XML)
  SPDX:      2.2, 2.3 (JSON, tag-value, RDF/XML), 3.0 (JSON-LD)

Output Formats:
  tui, json, ndjson, sarif, markdown, html, summary, table, side-by-side

Features:
  Semantic diff, fuzzy matching, vulnerability tracking, license analysis
